purpose: Close the highest-priority UK corpus target by structuring the locally available primary text of Arthur C. Cole's Studies in Microscopical Science, vols. I-II, without harmonizing source-level preparator attribution.

source.provenance: Local uploaded IA/DJVU text package; structured from full OCR, with OCR names normalized only where the printed reading is unambiguous.

attribution_guard.vol1: The preface credits the microscopical preparations issued with the work to Martin J. Cole.
attribution_guard.vol1_source_wording: The excellence of the microscopical preparations which have been issued with this work, is due to the skill of Mr. Martin J. Cole.
attribution_guard.vol2: The preface credits preparation jointly to Martin J. Cole and Arthur C. Cole.
attribution_guard.vol2_source_wording: The preparations were made by my son, Mr. Martin J. Cole (Instructor in Practical Microscopy at the Birkbeck Institution), and myself.
attribution_guard.rule: Do not collapse the two volume-level statements into a single maker attribution. Vol. I and vol. II carry different explicit responsibility statements.

preface_roles.articles: J. E. Ady wrote all but three articles
preface_roles.geology_articles: Professor Heddle: red and white syenites of Lairg and serpentine of Portsoy

volumes.first_preparation_anchor: No. 1 is headed 'L.Y.S. Pinna of Ear of Cow x 333. Double Stained in Logwood and Eosin.'
volumes.interpretive_result: Vol. I is a numbered preparation-text sequence that deliberately alternates or interleaves animal histology, plant histology and lithological sections. The preparation is part of the publication architecture, not an incidental illustration.

preface_roles.botanical_histology: David Houston, F.L.S., F.R.M.S., Birkbeck Institution
preface_roles.popular_studies: W. Fearnley and Frederick Greene assisted
preface_roles.preparations: Martin J. Cole and Arthur C. Cole jointly

volumes.contents_ocr_guard: The OCR table of contents loses or corrupts some lines although the preface says twelve short essays in each of the Animal and Botanical Histology sections. Only clearly recovered headings are listed here; no missing heading is reconstructed from sequence alone.
botanical_histology_headings_recovered: The Morphology of the Cell—The Cell
volumes.methods_layer: The volume explicitly contains a continuing 'Methods of Microscopical Research' section. Existing JRMS abstracts identify, among other instalments, mounting/material descriptions and preparation of Diatomaceae.
volumes.interpretive_result: Vol. II makes the division of labour explicit: essay authorship, drawings, preparation, and methods are separate roles. It therefore gives unusually strong primary evidence for a coordinated material-publication workflow.

corpus_crosswalk.existing_uk_corpus: JRMS summary/review records already abstract individual Cole instalments and preparation/method details, including R29639 for vol. II nos. 15-18 and methods parts IX-X.
corpus_crosswalk.new_value: The direct primary text closes volume-level architecture and responsibility statements that were only indirectly represented by review notices.
corpus_crosswalk.dedupe_rule: Do not duplicate JRMS abstracts as new source events; retain the primary Cole structure as a source-level complement.

open_gap: Later volumes III-IV remain outside this bounded task; no need to expand before a writing question requires them.
